manifest.name: MCP Atlassian
manifest.description: Model Context Protocol (MCP) server for Atlassian products (Confluence and Jira), for Cloud and Server/Data Center deployments. Lets an AI assistant search Jira with JQL, read issue details, create and update issues, and change an issue's status through its workflow transitions.

publications.verifiedBy: Image published under the repository owner's GitHub Container Registry namespace and documented in the project's installation guide.

supportedUseCases.title: Find and read Jira issues
supportedUseCases.description: Search issues with JQL (jira_search) and read one issue with its comments (jira_get_issue).

supportedUseCases.title: Update the status of a Jira issue
supportedUseCases.description: Move an issue through its workflow, for example to Done (jira_transition_issue).

supportedUseCases.title: Summarise Jira issues and sprints
supportedUseCases.description: Returns issue, sprint, and search data that the AI assistant summarises. The server supplies the data; the summary is written by the assistant's model.

supportedUseCases.title: Create and edit Jira issues
supportedUseCases.description: Create issues (jira_create_issue) and update their fields (jira_update_issue).

interfaces.description: Local MCP server started by the MCP client (the default). The same server also supports the sse and streamable-http transports for shared or multi-user deployments. Tools are discovered at runtime through tools/list.

embeddedComponents.name: jira_create_issue
embeddedComponents.description: Create an issue. Writes to Jira.

embeddedComponents.name: jira_update_issue
embeddedComponents.description: Update an issue's fields. Writes to Jira.

embeddedComponents.name: jira_transition_issue
embeddedComponents.description: Change an issue's status. Writes to Jira.

embeddedComponents.name: jira_get_sprint_issues
embeddedComponents.description: List the issues in a sprint (agile toolset).

setup.name: JIRA_URL
setup.description: Base URL of the Jira site, for example https://your-company.atlassian.net.

setup.name: JIRA_USERNAME
setup.description: Atlassian account email. Jira Cloud only, together with JIRA_API_TOKEN.

setup.name: JIRA_API_TOKEN
setup.description: Jira Cloud API token, created at id.atlassian.com/manage-profile/security/api-tokens.

setup.name: JIRA_PERSONAL_TOKEN
setup.description: Personal Access Token for Jira Server/Data Center, used instead of username and API token.

setup.name: READ_ONLY_MODE
setup.description: Set to true to disable all write operations (create, update, transition).

setup.name: TOOLSETS
setup.description: Restrict the tools offered, for example 'default' (about 35 core tools) or 'default,jira_agile'.

limitations: Not an official Atlassian product; maintained by an individual open-source maintainer.
Jira Server/Data Center is supported from version 8.14; Confluence Server/Data Center from 6.0.
Write tools (create, update, transition) are enabled unless READ_ONLY_MODE=true is set.
When TOOLSETS is not set, all toolsets are enabled (98 tools in total, Jira and Confluence).
Acts with the permissions of the Atlassian account whose token it is given.
The container image is documented with the floating tag 'latest'; pin a version for production.

costInformation.details: MIT-licensed open source. Requires existing Atlassian (Jira) licences.

manifest.name: PR-Agent
manifest.description: Open-source, AI-powered code review agent for pull requests. Reviews a pull request's changes and comments on code quality and possible issues (/review), suggests code improvements (/improve), writes a pull request description (/describe), and answers questions about the change (/ask). Works with GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, Azure DevOps, and Gitea.

publications.verifiedBy: The README names pragent/pr-agent as the image namespace for releases 0.34.2 and later.
The README's GitHub Action example uses the-pr-agent/pr-agent@main.

relations.evidence: README: 'This repository contains the open-source PR Agent Project. It is not the Qodo offering for open-source projects.'

supportedUseCases.title: Review the code quality of a pull request
supportedUseCases.description: The /review command comments on the changes, possible issues, and code quality.

supportedUseCases.title: Suggest code improvements
supportedUseCases.description: The /improve command proposes concrete code changes for the pull request.

supportedUseCases.title: Describe a pull request
supportedUseCases.description: The /describe command writes the pull request's title and description.

supportedUseCases.title: Answer questions about a pull request
supportedUseCases.description: The /ask command answers free-text questions about the change.

interfaces.description: GitHub Action the-pr-agent/pr-agent@main, triggered on pull_request opened and synchronize; it reads OPENAI_KEY and GITHUB_TOKEN from the workflow environment.
Comment commands on a pull request (/review, /improve, /describe, /ask), run by the GitHub Action, the GitHub App, or a webhook deployment.

embeddedComponents.name: /ask
embeddedComponents.description: Answer a question about the pull request.

runtime.detail: A GitHub Actions runner, triggered on pull_request opened and synchronize.
Python >=3.12; the GitHub provider needs the github extra.

setup.name: OPENAI_KEY
setup.description: API key for the model provider (OpenAI in the default example). Other providers are configured through LiteLLM settings.

setup.name: GITHUB_TOKEN
setup.description: GitHub token that lets PR-Agent read the pull request and post comments. In GitHub Actions, secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN.

limitations: Needs an external large language model; the pull request's code is sent to the configured model provider.
The README's GitHub Action example pins the floating reference @main; pin a release for production.
/help_docs is disabled since v0.36.1 pending a fix for a credential-exposure issue (issue 2445).
Community-maintained legacy project of Qodo; distinct from Qodo's commercial code review product.
Reviews are AI-generated suggestions and can be wrong; it does not approve or block merges by itself.

costInformation.details: The software is free (MIT). Each command makes a model API call, billed by the model provider.
